source_review.notes: Checked current Apache Flink checkpoint, savepoint, backend, local recovery, upgrade, schema, and recovery configuration documentation; current Kafka Streams state restore/high-availability documentation; the Beam runner guide; and MillWheel. All thirteen cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Version-specific mechanisms are attributed and separated from general manifest, compatibility, and recovery invariants.

evidence: Reviewed manifest M_n and position/state/timer/channel/effect components P_n,S_n,T_n,Q_n,E_n plus dependency graph D_n.
Checked Reach(R), incremental delta versus restore closure, phase durations, input/capacity rates lambda/mu, backlog N, and RPO/RTO terminology.
Checked MB versus MiB, seconds/minutes, records/s, checkpoint half-open positions, key-group counts, and dependency roots have explicit units/scopes.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical cut, encoded snapshot, completed manifest, primary/local copy, checkpoint/savepoint, process start, and recovered service are distinct.

evidence: Executed snapshot-selection-and-reachability with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced selected c3, restore 140 MB, live base/delta3, and orphan delta2.
Recomputed examples: 12 GB/300 MB/s=40 seconds; 400 MB/300 MB/s=1.33 seconds; serial RTO 360 seconds; 3.6M/(10k-8k)=1,800 seconds.
Recomputed Exercise 1 live A,B,D,E; orphan C; retained unique 230 MB; C4 restore 110 MB.
Recomputed Exercises 2–3: serial RTO 500 seconds=8m20s; 4.8M/(15k-12k)=1,600 seconds=26m40s; zero net capacity never catches up.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Calculations are ideal/base estimates; request tails, skew, compaction, retries, replication, and concurrent traffic remain excluded.

evidence: Verified restore eligibility requires completed, authentic, integrity-valid, policy-allowed, compatible manifest plus complete transitive dependency closure.
Checked GC eligibility as nonreachability from every retained/active/held root after grace and recheck, not simple parent deletion.
Verified catch-up N/(mu-lambda) requires mu>lambda and diverges/nonconverges at mu<=lambda.
Checked RTO additive expression is labeled an approximation only for serial stages; actual result is the dependency-aware critical path.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Incremental write size is deliberately not equated with restore read set or logical state size.

evidence: Reviewed newest valid/corrupt/incompatible/missing-key snapshots, incomplete roots, missing shared bases, partial local copies, old fallback, and exhausted source retention.
Reviewed zero/equal/insufficient catch-up capacity, slow/skewed shards, many small objects, request throttling, cold cache, compaction, timer bursts, and concurrent restore/GC.
Reviewed operator/state rename, old serializer bytes, key changes, key-group rescale, timer/window/time rules, backend/runtime downgrade, and sink transactions.
Reviewed forged manifests, corrupted objects, lost/rotated keys, unauthorized export/restore/delete, cross-tenant/region placement, stale owners, and disaster dependencies.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Integrity, compatibility, placement, source replay, effects, capacity, security, and lifecycle can invalidate an otherwise completed checkpoint.

evidence: Traced a completed cut through authenticated manifest, dependency traversal, selection, allocation, verified fetch/decode, shard ownership, source/sink reconciliation, replay, catch-up, validation, and cutover.
Checked source positions, state, timers, channel data, effects, topology, and schema are selected from one checkpoint identity.
Checked every state shard/key group maps exactly once with stale-owner fencing before processing/effects resume.
Checked remote primary remains complete while local copies/standbys/caches can only accelerate or stage restore under explicit durability.
invariant_checking.notes: Recovery completion requires correctness and freshness evidence rather than merely a running process.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from cut/manifest/closure through compatibility, placement, restore, reconciliation, capacity, lifecycle/security, and drills.
Checked manifest integrity composition binds an authenticated root to every immutable length/hash-verified dependency.
Checked restore completeness proof requires every shard exactly once plus matching source/effect metadata before exposure.
Checked GC race counterexample and requirement for stable marking, leases or grace/recheck under concurrent roots.
proof_review.notes: Current product mechanisms are examples beneath general graph, compatibility, ownership, and recovery proofs.

evidence: Audited uses of complete, immutable, durable, compatible, full, incremental, local, primary, exact, restored, recovered, and deleted.
Confirmed full snapshots may still be sharded and incremental/checkpoint completion does not imply independent or fast restore.
Confirmed RPO claims distinguish replayable managed state from source retention, nonreplayable inputs, outputs, and external decisions/effects.
Confirmed the fixture excludes hashes, transitive/racing DAGs, encryption, compatibility, placement, performance, replay, and effects.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No successful creation, object listing, process start, or local recovery is mislabeled as end-to-end recovery readiness.

evidence: Reviewed metrics for snapshot age, logical/full/incremental/unique/referenced bytes, objects/depth/sharing, throughput, keys/hashes, local coverage, standby/changelog lag, GC, and source margin.
Reviewed per-phase/per-shard RTO, fallback, bytes/requests, decode/open, placement, replay/backlog/rate, catch-up ETA, timers, effects, freshness, and semantic validation.
Confirmed no universal snapshot form, base frequency, retention, claim mode, local/standby policy, RPO/RTO, region, or catch-up ratio is prescribed.
Confirmed choices require production-scale restore drills, tail measurements, failure-domain/policy analysis, source/sink limits, compatibility evidence, and result reconciliation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The executable dependency example and arithmetic do not constitute distributed restore or disaster-recovery evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed logical/physical snapshots, manifests, dependency closure, full/incremental/changelog state, local/standby/disaggregated recovery, selection, staged restore, ownership, compatibility, timers/channels, source/sink reconciliation, RPO/RTO, catch-up, retention/GC, regional recovery, security, telemetry, and drills.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed manifest fields, immutable objects/hashes/keys, shared-base compaction, local fallback, newest-valid selection, old-byte/topology migration, shard fencing, source retention, sink transaction resolution, capacity, regional replication, protected recovery access, rollback, and production-scale drill evidence. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from representation and manifests through restore execution and operational proof. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover dependency reachability, incremental/read bytes, critical paths, fallback, RTO/catch-up, IDs, local fallback, regional publication, runnable selection, GC arithmetic, migration, and drills.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Flink/Kafka/Beam/MillWheel maintainer or researcher, database/storage/distributed-systems engineer, SRE/performance/disaster-recovery engineer, connector/sink owner, security/privacy/compliance/records authority, tenant/region owner, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
